audit_findings.title: The anchor assumes growth before the largest profit pool finishes normalizing
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 Plastics net income was $170.4 million, 61.8% of $275.9 million consolidated net income; first-half 2026 Plastics operating income excluding the $103.5 million settlement charge was $108.8 million, down $22.1 million or 16.9% from $130.9 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The disclosed 2026-2027 Plastics contraction should enter near-term OE before consolidated growth and terminal fade are applied.
audit_findings.evidence: We anticipate earnings from our Plastics segment will continue to decline through 2027 until such time that product pricing is expected to stabilize.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated forecast mismatch: the base and bull cases increase OE immediately even though the filing forecasts continued decline through 2027 and first-half 2026 results confirm material ongoing normalization. Because Plastics supplied most 2025 earnings, correcting the first two forecast years is reasonably capable of eliminating the base case's $4.05-per-share premium to the $89.79 market price.
audit_findings.action: Build segment-level 2026-2027 Plastics revenue, resin-cost and margin forecasts from filed guidance and results, combine them with Electric and Manufacturing forecasts, and rerun all scenarios before applying the terminal fade.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved antitrust and DOJ exposure is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: U.S. settlements total $103.5 million pretax and $77.2 million after the disclosed $26.3 million tax benefit; $30.0 million was funded after 2026-06-30 and is absent from the June cash/STI bridge; Canadian litigation and DOJ exposure are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The known post-quarter cash payment reduces bridge cash, while any additional Canadian judgment, DOJ fine, defense cost or lasting margin effect reduces the bridge or future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: At this time, we are unable to determine the likelihood of an outcome or estimate a range of reasonably possible losses, if any, arising from the class action complaints in the United States and Canada or the DOJ investigation.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing supersedes the finding's premise for the U.S. classes: a $103.5 million liability was recorded and the settlements were funded. However, the June-based $333.703 million cash/STI bridge still includes the $30.0 million paid in July, a demonstrated $0.71-per-share timing overstatement. That amount alone is only 0.8% of base equity value and would not reverse the base conclusion. The Canadian case and DOJ investigation remain unresolved and unreserved, but the record supplies no loss range, so their materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Reduce June bridge cash by the July $30.0 million funding, confirm final court approval and tax realization, and obtain filed loss estimates or scenario-supported exposures for the Canadian case and DOJ investigation before rerunning the bridge and Plastics OE.

audit_findings.title: Required new financing may introduce interest costs missing from the 2025 equity-OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: The 2026 issuance adds $170.0 million of debt with computed annual contractual interest of $9.558 million, equal to 3.7% of the $259.9 million OE anchor; additional required financing is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-OE model, incremental interest expense and any share issuance must reduce future OE or increase fully diluted shares; capitalized interest must enter OE when the associated assets begin operating.
audit_findings.evidence: Debt financing will be required in the five-year period from 2026 through 2030 to refinance maturing debt and to finance our planned capital investments.
audit_findings.explanation: The financing is no longer hypothetical: $100 million was issued at 5.33% and $70 million at 6.04%. Mechanically growing the 2025 after-interest anchor does not separately charge this new interest. The known gross run-rate is close to the base case's 4.5% valuation premium over market price, and further financing is required, so the omission is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion. Regulatory recovery and earnings from the financed assets may offset part of the cost but must be modeled rather than assumed.
audit_findings.action: Add a year-by-year debt schedule covering the $170.0 million issuance and remaining capital-plan funding, including rates, capitalization periods, tax effects and regulatory recovery, then rerun equity OE and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Customer refund obligations may not be represented in the mechanical OE forecast
audit_findings.magnitude: At 2026-06-30 regulatory liabilities were $329.550 million and regulatory assets were $111.760 million, a computed net liability of $217.790 million or $5.13 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Refunds, rate reductions, PTC credits and removal spending reduce future OE as settled; recoverable regulatory assets increase future OE. Only residual amounts not captured in OE belong in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Regulatory liabilities generally represent amounts to be refunded to customers or amounts currently collected from customers for future costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The balance is not automatically a dollar-for-dollar debt deduction because it contains deferred taxes, removal obligations, PTC refunds and other items settling over different periods, with regulatory assets providing offsets. Nevertheless, the $217.8 million net balance exceeds the approximately $171.7 million base-equity premium over market capitalization. A mechanical growth forecast with no runoff schedule is therefore reasonably capable of assigning customer funds to shareholders.
audit_findings.action: Roll forward each June 2026 regulatory asset and liability by expected refund or recovery year, map the associated revenue, tax and removal cash flows into OE, and rerun the valuation with only genuinely non-operating residuals placed in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The unconsolidated mining VIE creates an additional claim ahead of equity
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum filed exposure is $35 million, equal to $0.82 per diluted share and 0.9% of the $3.985 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An early Coyote/LSA termination could create a one-time equity claim through asset purchases and assumption or repayment of CCMC loans, leases and reclamation obligations.
audit_findings.evidence: In the event the contract is terminated prior to the end of the term due to certain events, OTP’s maximum loss exposure, as a result of its involvement with CCMC, could be as high as $ 35 million, or OTP’s 35 % share of CCMC’s unrecovered costs as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation is contingent rather than a demonstrated current liability. Even treating the entire filed maximum as an immediate unrecovered equity deduction would reduce base value from $93.84 to about $93.02 per share, still above the $89.79 price, and would not change the bear, base, bull or buy-below conclusions. This assessment is limited to the stated CCMC VIE exposure and does not cover separate Coyote plant stranded costs.
audit_findings.action: Confirm through the current IRP, LSA termination provisions and commission orders that $35 million remains the maximum unrecovered CCMC exposure; rerun only if a trigger occurs or a larger filed estimate emerges.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded postretirement claims require reconciliation to owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed undiscounted postretirement payments total $70 million, equal to $1.65 per diluted share and 1.8% of base equity value; 2025 company-funded ESSRP and healthcare cash payments were $5.563 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash benefit payments should reduce OE when paid, offset by any regulatory recovery; alternatively, an unfunded residual can enter the bridge once, without duplicating expense already retained in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Postretirement benefit obligations include estimated cash expenditures for the payment of retiree medical and life insurance benefits and supplemental pension benefits under our unfunded Executive Survivor and Supplemental Retirement Plan (ESSRP), but do not include amounts to fund our noncontributory funded pension plan, as we are not currently required to make any contributions to that plan.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting-versus-cash reconciliation is unresolved, but the filed payment schedule bounds the identified claim. Even an overly conservative immediate deduction of the entire undiscounted $70 million would reduce base value to about $92.19 per share and leave it above the $89.79 market price; actual present value should be lower because $40 million is due beyond five years and regulatory recovery may offset part. It therefore cannot change the stated valuation conclusion on the supplied scale.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile ESSRP and retiree-health cash payments against service cost, nonservice components, regulatory recovery and the OE construction; correct any timing mismatch once and verify that no liability is deducted again in the bridge.
